San Francisco, California · off the bike

San Francisco off the bike: record stores, bookshops, bars

What to do in San Francisco with the afternoon after the ride.

San Francisco off the bike: record stores, bookshops, bars, listed

What do you need?

  1. Amoeba Music San Francisco

    Zone 3, the Upper Haight near Golden Gate Park, inside the old Park Bowl bowling alley.

    • Record store
    • 1855 Haight St. San Francisco, CA 94117
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Amoeba Music San Francisco

    New and used vinyl and CDs, a DVD room it calls the biggest in the Bay Area, and free in-store shows. Open 11 to 7 every day, so it works after a park and Sunset Dunes loop.

  2. City Lights Booksellers & Publishers

    Zone 6, North Beach, about a mile and a half from City Hall.

    • Bookstore
    • 261 Columbus Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94133
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about City Lights Booksellers & Publishers

    The bookstore and press the poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti founded in 1953, still selling and publishing. Open 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day, so it’s the stop after dinner at Original Joe’s, a few blocks away.

  3. Ferry Plaza Farmers Market

    • Market
    • One Ferry Building, San Francisco, California 94111
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Ferry Plaza Farmers Market

    Zone 6, the Ferry Building on the Embarcadero, about 2 miles from City Hall, where Butterlap (Wednesdays, 7:00 pm) gathers and the Sausalito and Larkspur ferries land. Foodwise runs it year-round, rain or shine: Tuesday and Thursday 10 to 2, Saturday 8 to 2, with about 70 farmers and 50 food makers. Saturday is the big one, out front and on the back plaza over the bay, so it works after a morning ride; no bike parking stated.

  4. GLBT Historical Society Museum

    Zone 6, the Castro, where Different Spokes’ Jersey Ride (2nd Saturday of the month, 8:45 am) leaves from.

    • Museum
    • 4127 18th Street, San Francisco, CA 94114
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about GLBT Historical Society Museum

    One long-term show, Queer Past Becomes Present, plus rotating ones; the audioguide runs about 35 minutes, so give it an hour. Open 11 to 5 Tuesday to Sunday, closed 1 to 1:30 and all day Monday; $10, $6 discounted, free the first Wednesday of the month (Oct 2026).

  5. Splitrock Tap & Wheel (the taproom)

    • Bar
    • 2020 Sir Francis Drake Blvd., Fairfax, CA 94930
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Splitrock Tap & Wheel (the taproom)

    Zone 2, Fairfax, the post-ride bar in Marin: the taproom and café side of the bike shop where Marin Cyclists’ Point Reyes Station ride (Saturdays, 8:45 am) meets; the Mt. Tam loop in this guide starts in Fairfax too. The café runs 11 a.m. to 8:30 or 9 p.m., per its own site; the shop is open every day 10 to 6. The business filed for Chapter 11 in April 2026 and said it will keep operating (WhatNow, April 14, 2026), so call (415) 721-7644 before you plan the evening around it.

  6. Castro Theatre

    Zone 6, the Castro, about a mile and a half from City Hall.

    • Venue
    • 429 Castro St, San Francisco, CA 94114
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Castro Theatre

    The neighborhood’s theater reopened February 6, 2026 after a $41 million renovation. Another Planet runs it, mostly concerts, with films and comedy too. Buy tickets online; the box office opens 30 minutes before doors on show nights. The evening plan for anyone sleeping at Beck’s.

Checked October 3, 2026. No paid placements. Businesses open and close; call before you count on anyone.
